title: Managing Product Delivery in Context

header.html: 4.5.1 apply managing product delivery: activities, inputs and outputs, roles and responsibilities, how the practices are applied; 4.5.2 analyze whether the activities, roles and responsibilities are effective and fit for purpose, considering tailoring, the practices, and the purpose and objectives of the process
the official PRINCE2 7 Practitioner syllabus (PeopleCert, version 7.2)

toc.title: Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

html:
1Purpose, objectives and the principles it serves

Managing product delivery is the team manager's process. It is the formal link between the project manager and the team manager. The figure shows the three activities.

Purpose: control the link between the project manager and the team manager by placing formal requirements on accepting, executing and delivering project work.

Objectives: work on products is authorized and agreed; the team knows what is expected, including effort, cost and time; products are delivered to the expected quality and within tolerance; progress information reaches the project manager at an agreed frequency.

Principle How it shows up here
Focus on products The work package asks for defined products with quality criteria
Manage by exception The work package has tolerances; a forecast breach goes to the project manager
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships Team managers report to the project manager, not to the board
Continued business justification Unapproved extras that add cost are not delivered
Learn from experience Lessons from the work are passed on
Exam tip

. The team manager agrees the work package before accepting it, including the tolerances. An option where the team starts without agreement, or ignores the tolerances, is a red flag.

2Activities, inputs and outputs

The names below give the general idea; check the Official Book's wording for the activities.

Activity What the team manager does
Accept a work package Reviews the work package description; agrees products, tolerances, quality and reporting; plans the work, with a team plan if needed
Execute a work package Builds the products; applies the quality method; sends checkpoint reports; raises issues and risks
Deliver a work package Gets products approved, hands them over as agreed and tells the project manager the work is complete
Flow Main items
Inputs The authorized work package: work package description, product descriptions, tolerances, constraints, reporting needs
Outputs Checkpoint reports; the team plan; quality records; completed products with approvals; issues, risks and lessons raised to the project manager
Exam tip

. Team managers report to the project manager, not to the board. The board hears about the stage through the highlight report, which the project manager writes.

3Roles

Role Area of focus in this process
Team manager Responsible: accepts, executes and delivers the work package; agrees tolerances; reports
Project manager Authorizes and agrees the work package; receives reports and products; keeps control
Team members Do the work to the quality asked
Senior supplier Makes supplier resources available; is accountable for supplier quality
Senior user Provides users for reviews and approvals when needed
Project assurance Checks quality and progress independently
Change authority Decides changes that the project manager brings as issues
Project support Keeps product status and configuration records

Check the book's roles table for this process. The general rule: the project manager authorizes and the team manager delivers.

4How the practices are applied

Practice How it is applied in managing product delivery
Quality Product descriptions guide the work; quality methods are applied; quality records and approvals are kept
Plans The team plan fits the work package and its tolerances
Risk The team manager reports risks and manages those delegated
Issues Changes, problems and concerns go to the project manager; the team does not approve changes
Progress Checkpoint reports at the agreed frequency; early warning of a tolerance breach
Organization Reporting lines are clear, including supplier teams under the commercial management approach
Business case Deliver what is needed for the benefits; no extras

5Judging a scenario

Effective approach Red flag: not fit for purpose
The team manager agrees the work package, including tolerances, and negotiates if it is unrealistic Accepting an unrealistic work package silently, or starting before agreeing it
Checkpoint reports at the agreed frequency show status, forecast, issues and risks No reports until the work is done
Quality records show products were checked against the product description and approved Delivery with no evidence of checks
Changes are raised to the project manager as issues Unapproved changes or extra features inside the work package
A forecast breach of the work package tolerance is raised at once Carrying on and hoping to catch up
Completion is confirmed to the project manager and products are handed over as agreed Products passed straight to users or the board

Tailoring changes the form, not the agreement:

  • Supplier teams: the work package matches the contract and the commercial management approach. The supplier keeps its own methods and reports in an agreed format.
  • Agile delivery: the team uses its own iterations and backlog. The work package states the products, priorities and tolerances (often fixed time and cost, flexible scope), and team data can serve as checkpoint information.
  • Small projects: the project manager may also be the team manager. The agreement is lighter, but what, when and how much are still clear.
  • Sustainability, digital and data: the work package can state sustainability or data protection needs for the products.
Exam tip

. A team can use its own method but must still agree the work package, report to the project manager and meet the quality asked. A supplier is not exempt from the process.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Wei Chen's team receives a work package to build the berth-permit form in four weeks. Wei knows the team has only half the staff needed, but starts work without comment, hoping to catch up. Was this an appropriate action for the team manager to take, and why?

  • AYes, because a team manager must accept any work package given
  • BYes, because the team can usually catch up inside the work package
  • CNo, because the team manager must first ask the board to approve it
  • DNo, because the work package must be agreed as achievable before starting
Show the answer

Answer: D. Accepting a work package means agreeing that the products, effort and tolerances are achievable, and an unrealistic one must be raised with the project manager first.

S2The harbor master mentions an extra online payment feature, and Wei Chen's team adds it to the work package without telling the project manager. Was this an appropriate action for the team manager to take, and why?

  • ANo, because changes must go to the project manager as an issue
  • BNo, because the senior supplier must approve every added feature
  • CYes, because a request from a senior user is enough authority
  • DYes, because extra features always increase the value of the products
Show the answer

Answer: A. Changes are handled through the issues practice, so the team manager raises it with the project manager and the change authority decides.

S3Halfway through a work package, Wei Chen's team forecasts that it will exceed the agreed time tolerance by three days. The next weekly checkpoint report is in five days. What should Wei do?

  • AWait for the next checkpoint report and explain the delay there
  • BAsk the project board to extend the work package tolerance
  • CReduce the quality checks on the products to save the three days
  • DTell the project manager at once so that action can be agreed
Show the answer

Answer: D. A forecast breach of work package tolerance is escalated promptly to the project manager (manage by exception), not held for the next report.

S4Delta Software's team has finished a work package and every product was checked. Who is responsible for telling the project manager that the work package is complete and for handing the products over?

  • ALena Kovac, the senior supplier
  • BWei Chen, the team manager
  • CAisha Bello, the assurance lead
  • DJon Park, project support
Show the answer

Answer: B. The team manager delivers the work package and confirms completion to the project manager.

S5Sam Okafor and Wei Chen agree that Wei will report on the progress of a work package each week, with forecasts and issues. Which management product does Wei send?

  • AEnd project report
  • BException report
  • CCheckpoint report
  • DEnd stage report
Show the answer

Answer: C. The checkpoint report goes from the team manager to the project manager at the agreed frequency.

S6Delta Software's team uses its own sprint method. Wei Chen agrees the products, tolerances and weekly checkpoint information with Sam Okafor, and the team plans its own sprints. Was this appropriate tailoring, and why?

  • AYes, because the work package is agreed and the team keeps its method
  • BYes, because an agile team does not need an agreed work package
  • CNo, because the project manager must approve every sprint task
  • DNo, because a supplier team must follow the project manager's methods
Show the answer

Answer: A. The work package, tolerances and reporting are agreed, which is what the process requires, while the method is the team's choice.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the purpose of managing product delivery?

Show the answer

To control the link between the project manager and the team manager with formal requirements for accepting, executing and delivering work.

R2Whose process is managing product delivery?

Show the answer

The team manager's.

R3Name the three activities.

Show the answer

Accept a work package, execute a work package and deliver a work package.

R4Which report does the team manager send to the project manager during execution?

Show the answer

The checkpoint report.

R5What should the team manager do with a change that comes up inside a work package?

Show the answer

Raise it with the project manager as an issue.

R6What shows that products were checked before delivery?

Show the answer

Quality records, with the approvals.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Purpose formal link between project manager and team manager: accept, execute, deliver
Activities accept, execute and deliver a work package
Inputs the authorized work package with product descriptions and tolerances
Outputs checkpoint reports, team plan, quality records, completed products
Roles team manager responsible; project manager authorizes and receives
Effective agreed work package, checkpoints, quality records, no unapproved changes
Red flags silent acceptance, hidden slippage, extras, reporting to the board
Tailoring supplier and agile teams keep their method but still agree and report
